title: Self-Cleaning Solutions for Photovoltaics, Progress and Limitations
content: Photovoltaic [PV] systems are fully sustainable energy sources. The PV market in the EU-27 countries is expanding rapidly. The PV market is projected to grow from USD 613.57 billion in 2025 to USD 968.32 billion in 2030, at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR). This publication aims to review and present modern self-cleaning and anti-soiling coatings suitable for protecting PV. The article discusses the current state of knowledge regarding superhydrophobic, hydrophilic, photocatalytic, oleopho-bic, anti-adhesive, and amphiphobic coatings. In technical applications, multiple mechanisms are often combined—for instance, a photocatalytic coating with a super-hydrophilic effect. This analysis aims to indicate limitations of the existing solutions and directions for further research as well as possibilities of improving the durability of self-cleaning systems for the protection of PV modules as a promising tool for re-ducing operational losses. However, it must be emphasized that their effectiveness depends heavily on the climate, the type of soiling, coating durability, and the eco-nomics of system maintenance.
